summary: Practise surveillance analysis, study design and population-health reporting. Explore epidemiologist training and build usable course outputs.
lede: Epidemiology training helps public health officers, surveillance analysts and health-programme leads turn population-health data into usable findings. Participants practise checking line-list quality and calculating incidence and prevalence, comparing observational study designs and interpreting basic risk measures. They also learn to communicate findings, limitations and evidence-linked recommendations in concise action briefs; the course focuses on practical foundations rather than advanced statistical modelling.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who collect, analyse or act on population-health information and need to make epidemiological findings clear and usable. It suits people building foundational capability as well as practitioners who want a more consistent approach to surveillance measures, study design and reporting.
prerequisites: No coding is required. Familiarity with health, surveillance or population data will help you work through the exercises.
topics: Statistics & data analysis (SPSS, Stata, R, Python)
